text:
lia: heads up — last night's soft-shed spike highlighted some gaps in how we classify degraded capacity. thinking we should land a small taxonomy + admit API surface so schedulers and SRE can play nicely. thoughts?

maria: agree. saw ~15% soft-shed events between 02:10-02:45 UTC, mostly p95 tail on long-seq tenants. a taxonomy would help. quick q: is this for runtime-only or include ingress/admission?

lia: both. runtime needs signal semantics but admission should expose a compact contract: allow|soft_reject|hard_reject + reason + optional fallback_variant. keeping it small helps cross-team use.

ashley: can you sketch the fields? e.g. `soft_reject` might include severity and suggested backoff? also how do we prevent thundering herd on fallback variants? :thinking_face:

lia: sketch below — simple JSON response from admission service:```json
{
  "decision": "soft_reject",
  "reason": "tenant_rate_exceeded",
  "severity": "medium",
  "fallback_variant": "gpt-small-quant",
  "retry_after_s": 4
}```
This keeps runtime/scheduler decoupled: admission returns the policy, scheduler picks a path (route to fallback, queue, throttle).

kevin: I like it. A couple tradeoffs: (1) coupling to named model variants in admission builds a surface area that needs sync with model catalog; (2) we need idempotent signals so repeated admits don't keep flipping clients.

lia: good point. Maybe admission returns a token + TTL for the soft_reject window so schedulers can dedupe. e.g. `soft_id: abc123, ttl_s: 30`

maria: operationally we also need observability fields. If we have `policy_id` and `signal_version`, we can roll out new heuristics without losing continuity in dashboards. Also include `confidence`? small float.

ashley: what about abuse signals? We should avoid punishing noisy tenants incorrectly. Are we using historical burst rate vs. short-term gradients?

sam: for abuse detection we currently compute an abuse_score on the path before admission. Could surface `abuse_score` in the admit response and have a threshold mapping to `hard_reject`. But important: the threshold mapping should be owned by security, not runtime.

lia: agreed. Proposed mapping: abuse_score >= 0.9 -> hard_reject; 0.6-0.9 -> probation/soft_reject; <0.6 -> normal. But keep the numeric score opaque to external callers; internal teams can use it for triage.

kevin: another UX consideration: fallback_variant routing needs rate limits of its own. If we route 100 tenants to a smaller model, that model may saturate and cause cascading failures. We should surface recommended capacity and an estimated cost delta in the admit response so router can make an informed routing decision.

lia: good call. new proposed fields to add: `estimated_delta_tps`, `estimated_cost_multiplier`. both optional.

maria: rollout plan? I'd prefer a canary: start with 10% of tenants and a dry-run flag where admit returns `decision: dry_run` and we only log telemetry + alert on regressions. then flip to enforced.

ashley: agree. plus a kill-switch in console to disable enforcement per-region. Also we should mock failure modes in chaos tests: controller crash, inconsistent model catalog, and stale soft_id tokens.

sam: test fixtures: synthetic tenant with long-seq workload + aggressive burster. validate that soft_reject path yields acceptable latency and no cache poisoning. add telemetry asserts for no more than X% fallthrough to hard_reject in canary.

lia: ok next: interface boundary doc. I'll draft a one-pager: API (fields), signal semantics (ttl, idempotence), rollout steps, telemetry keys, and playbook entries. Action items: 1) Lia to draft RFC PR by EOD Friday. 2) Maria to add telemetry dashboard skeleton. 3) Kevin to add router simulation for fallback saturation. 4) Ashley to add chaos tests. 5) Sam to review abuse thresholds with security.

ashley: tiny nit — name suggestion: call the overall feature `soft-capacity-triage` so logs/search stay consistent. :thumbsup:

kevin: thumbs up. on simulation I'll prototype a toy that replays real traces and measures tail latencies when routing to fallback pool. will share links in thread.

maria: I'll put a dashboard PR targeting `infra-telemetry` with placeholders: `soft_shed_count`, `soft_shed_ratio`, `fallback_routing_count`, `fallback_drop_rate`, `soft_id_collision_rate`.

lia: perfect. If nobody objects, I'll open the RFC and include the sample admit JSON, rollout plan, and test matrix.

ashley: no objections from me. Thanks!

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary window created for `soft-capacity-triage` 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z -> 2026-04-02T04:00:00Z (for teams: eng-platform, eng-infra, eng-runtime).

lia: thanks — linking the RFC draft when ready.

kevin: ping me when the RFC has simulation links.

sam: I'll coordinate threshold review with security next week.

maria: adding the dashboard card now. done.

lia: closing the loop — RFC opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/4287 (dry_run + admit API). please review when you get a chance.
